text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.62% today to $137.38, extending a rally that has gained 5.18% over two weeks. The move follows U.S. crude oil breaking back above $100 a barrel today for the first time since May, driven by escalating Iran-U.S. tensions that have raised fears of Middle East supply disruptions. As an oil and gas producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices climb—higher oil prices translate into higher revenues from the company's own production.

The stock's two-week rally reflects a shift in the energy market's outlook. Escalating geopolitical risk in the Persian Gulf, combined with investor appetite for energy assets (despite limited bargains), has kept oil elevated and kept buyers interested in energy companies whose earnings depend on crude prices remaining strong.
